title: Plane-Wave Photon-Fock Cavity QED-DFT: Chiral-Cavity-Induced Topology in Graphene
abstract: We develop an explicit plane-wave (PW) $\times$ photon-Fock approach to the quantized, velocity-gauge Pauli--Fierz Hamiltonian for periodic, first-principles calculations: because the quantized vector potential is spatially uniform, the light--matter coupling reduces to an operator-valued shift of the crystal momentum, $K\to K+\hat{\mathbf A}/c$, and the existing plane-wave machinery of ordinary solid-state DFT is reused essentially unchanged. This PW$\times$Fock construction puts first-principles cavity QED of periodic solids on the same footing as the Fock-space coupled-cluster and configuration-interaction methods already developed for molecules, opening hitherto inaccessible systems---materials in a linear or chiral cavity, in particular---to first-principles plane-wave calculations. We illustrate the method with monolayer graphene in linear and chiral cavities, obtaining a polarization-selective Haldane gap together with the corresponding density-of-states, real-space, and circular-dichroism optical signatures. A full Brillouin-zone Berry-curvature calculation confirms the topological character of the chiral-cavity gap directly: the occupied manifold carries a quantized Chern number that steps through a non-monotonic sequence, $C=1\to3\to{-1}\to1\to2\to{-1}\to1$, with two narrow, sign-reversed windows---a property of extended, vacuum-dressed matter with no counterpart in a finite molecular system.
summary: The authors present a novel plane-wave approach to calculate cavity QED effects in periodic solids, using graphene coupled to optical cavities. They demonstrate that a chiral cavity induces a topologically non-trivial Haldane gap, characterized by a quantized, sign-changing Chern number. This method establishes a powerful theoretical tool for engineering topological phases in materials using photonic structures.
main_problem: Developing a first-principles method to study cavity Quantum Electrodynamics (QED) in periodic solids, specifically addressing the coupling between electrons and quantized cavity photons.
main_result: The method successfully calculates the topological character of the chiral-cavity gap, showing the occupied manifold carries a quantized Chern number that steps through a non-monotonic sequence.
method: An explicit plane-wave (PW) $	imes$ photon-Fock approach is developed, reusing existing plane-wave DFT machinery by modifying the crystal momentum ($\mathbf{K} 	o \mathbf{K} + \hat{\mathbf{A}}/c$).
model_or_system: The study uses monolayer graphene placed in linear or chiral optical cavities, modeled via the non-relativistic Pauli–Fierz Hamiltonian. The approach extends molecular QED methods to periodic, first-principles calculations.
key_observables: Quantized Chern number, polarization-selective Haldane gap, density-of-states, and circular-dichroism.
important_parameters: Coupling strength ($A_0/c$), cavity polarization (linear vs. chiral), and the Brillouin zone momentum ($\mathbf{K}$).
main_assumptions: The method is formulated at the Kohn–Sham (mean-field) level and is valid in the long-wavelength (dipole) approximation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the band structure (polariton replicas) for different cavity couplings, showing the gap opening in the chiral case and the Berry curvature over the Brillouin zone confirming the Chern number sequence.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the PW$	imes$Fock formalism, applies it to graphene in cavities, calculates topological invariants (Chern number) via Berry curvature, and analyzes measurable optical signatures like circular dichroism.
why_interesting: This work bridges solid-state DFT with cavity QED by providing a rigorous, first-principles framework to calculate topological phases induced by light-matter coupling in extended materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Polariton band structure at intermediate coupling (A0/c = 0.04, ω = 2 eV, M = 3), each panel referenced to its own Fermi level. (a)–(c): full-window bands, cavity-free/linear/chiral. (d)–(f): Dirac-point zoom. Color is w0 [Eq. (6)]; blue 1, matter-like; red 0, photon-dressed. The linear cavity leaves the Dirac crossing gapless (e), as symmetry requires (see text); the chiral (Haldane) gap (129 meV, dashed ellipse, f) opens with the branches still matter-like at K, the real hybridization occurring off-K where a different photon replica crosses the cone.

FIG. 2. Cavity-induced density change at A0/c = 0.04, linear color scale. (a) Cavity-free density n2D(x, y), z-integrated. (b) Linear-cavity minus cavity-free difference ∆n2D (blue/red = depletion/accumulation), max |∆n2D| = 1.619×10−2 e/bohr2. (c) Chiral-cavity minus cavity-free difference, same scale, max |∆n2D| = 2.024 × 10−2 e/bohr2. White circles mark the four carbon atoms.

FIG. 3. Density of states and dielectric response at A0/c = 0.04. (a) DOS; “total” sums all four Fock sectors, “matter” is the w0-weighted curve. (b) Absorption Im ¯ε(ω). (c) Linear dichroism |ε2,xx −ε2,yy|. (d) Circular dichroism 2 Im ε2,xy.

FIG. 4. Chern number of the occupied eight-band manifold, chiral cavity, across 29 independently converged couplings. Blue markers: C = 1, 2, 3; red markers: the two sign-reversed C = −1 notches, each ≲1×10−4 wide in A0/c and each imme- diately preceded by a jump to a higher-C plateau (shaded). The red diamond at A0/c = 0.05025 is independently con- firmed on four meshes spanning 60–9880 k-points (Supple- mental Material [88]). Berry-curvature maps for representa- tive couplings are shown in Fig. 5.

FIG. 5. Berry curvature of the occupied eight-band manifold over the full Brillouin zone, chiral cavity, at (a) A0/c = 0.04 (C = 1) and (b) A0/c = 0.05 (C = 2), the two original anchor couplings. Dotted lines mark the folded Dirac points K, K′

Spintronics.note: The new paper explicitly calculates cavity QED effects in graphene using a first-principles method, directly overlapping with the theme of cavity QED in solid-state systems, even if the specific focus is topological rather than magnetic.
